items.q: What is the cheapest Klaviyo alternative for a small list?
items.a: At the smallest sizes, it's close. Mailchimp's Essentials plan starts at $13 a month, a bit below Klaviyo's $20 entry price for roughly the same few hundred contacts, though Mailchimp's price moves in fixed contact bands rather than a smooth scale. Kit's free plan goes further: it costs nothing at all for up to 10,000 subscribers, well past Klaviyo's 250-active-profile free ceiling, but that free tier has no automation flows, so it only stays cheapest for a list that's happy sending plain broadcasts. ActiveCampaign skips a free plan entirely in favor of a 14-day trial, then starts around $15 a month billed annually for 1,000 contacts. None of the three include Klaviyo's native SMS or its store-specific flows, so a genuinely small, non-ecommerce list is where the savings are real; a store leaning on those features usually spends the difference rebuilding what it gave up.

items.q: Which Klaviyo alternative publishes SMS, MMS or WhatsApp rates you can check before signing up?
items.a: GoHighLevel is the clearest option here. Its help center publishes exact per-message rates for outbound SMS, MMS and WhatsApp templates, the same way Klaviyo does for standard US SMS, so you can price a texting-heavy list before committing to a plan. Klaviyo's own calculator, by contrast, showed no usable rate for MMS, WhatsApp or RCS at any tier checked, only its standard SMS rate. Of the other three alternatives, Mailchimp sells SMS and MMS as an add-on that needs an application and a monthly credit purchase, with no flat rate published anywhere on its pricing or comparison pages; ActiveCampaign's SMS add-on pricing is visible only after you've already signed up and logged in; and Kit has no SMS or MMS product at all. If texting cost certainty matters as much as email does, GoHighLevel is the only one of the four that gives you a number before you start.

items.q: Which Klaviyo alternative has the strongest built-in automation and CRM?
items.a: ActiveCampaign is the one built specifically around marketing automation with a CRM included, not layered on as an add-on: every paid plan, Starter included, already ships with both, starting around $15 a month billed annually for 1,000 contacts. That's a different model from Klaviyo, which charges its Email-plan price whether or not you use Composer, Customer Hub or any other add-on, and never bundles a full CRM at any tier. GoHighLevel is worth naming too: its $97 Starter plan bundles a CRM, a funnel and site builder, and usage-priced email and SMS into one subscription, aimed more at an agency or a business that wants marketing, sales and client management under one login. Pick ActiveCampaign for automation-first email with a light CRM attached; pick GoHighLevel when client management matters as much as the email does.

items.q: Does any Klaviyo alternative offer an annual-billing discount?
items.a: Yes, several do, and Klaviyo itself doesn't: every self-serve Klaviyo plan bills monthly only, with no annual toggle anywhere on its pricing calculator. Kit gives two free months on annual billing on both its paid plans, starting from its $39 Creator plan, with no contact-count minimum to unlock that discount. Mailchimp's annual pre-pay saves about 15%, available on every tier of its $350 Premium plan from the start, though on Essentials and Standard that same discount only appears once your contact list passes 10,000 contacts. ActiveCampaign's public pricing page shows only annual-billing rates to begin with, so its listed prices already assume a yearly commitment rather than a discount layered on a monthly one. GoHighLevel offers annual billing too, at ten months' price for the year.

items.q: Will my Klaviyo flows work the same way on a different platform?
items.a: No, not automatically, and that's the part a plain data export doesn't solve. Klaviyo's welcome, abandoned-cart and post-purchase flows are triggered by its own read of a connected store's order and browsing events, not by a static list, so the trigger logic itself has to be rebuilt inside whichever tool replaces it, using that tool's own store integration. A spreadsheet of names, emails and past purchases travels fine; the automation that acted on that data does not. Budget real time for this if flows are central to how you email today: recreating a five-step abandoned-cart sequence is a rebuild project, not a file import, whichever of Mailchimp, Kit, ActiveCampaign or GoHighLevel you move to. Test each rebuilt flow against a few real scenarios before turning off its Klaviyo equivalent, rather than assuming a like-for-like recreation behaves identically the first time.

items.q: Which Klaviyo alternative fits an agency running several client accounts?
items.a: GoHighLevel is built specifically for that job. Its Starter plan runs $97 a month for one business with up to 3 sub-accounts, and every plan includes unlimited users, so an agency runs several clients' CRM, funnels, sites and email or SMS marketing from one login instead of paying Klaviyo's per-client Email-plan price for each account separately. ActiveCampaign is worth a look too, if the priority is email automation specifically: every paid plan, Starter included, already bundles marketing automation and a CRM, so client work doesn't need separate add-on purchases the way Klaviyo's Composer, Customer Hub and Social Marketing do. Neither one replicates Klaviyo's specific read of a Shopify or WooCommerce client's order history, so an ecommerce-focused agency should weigh that loss against what it saves by consolidating tools onto one platform.

items.q: Is Klaviyo's free plan more generous than its competitors', or is it the other way around?
items.a: It depends which limit you'd hit first. Klaviyo's free plan covers up to 250 active profiles and 500 email sends a month, plus a small monthly allowance of SMS and Composer AI usage, though full email support only lasts 60 days after signup. Kit's free plan covers up to 10,000 subscribers, well beyond Klaviyo's ceiling, with unlimited broadcasts, forms and landing pages, though it excludes the automation flows and email sequences a growing list usually wants. Mailchimp's free plan is the smallest of the three, capped at 250 contacts and 500 sends a month, with support ending after 30 days. A store already integrated with Shopify or WooCommerce gets more from staying on Klaviyo's free tier, since that integration is the point of the product; a newsletter sender with a bigger list and no automation needs gets more runway from Kit's.
